cohort: 3,242 low-risk singleton pregnancies delivered at the Department of Obstetrics of the University Hospital of Cologne between 2017 and 2022
finding: In low-risk singleton pregnancies, advanced gestational age was associated with higher rates of secondary caesarean sections, lower rates of spontaneous vaginal deliveries, higher rates of meconium-stained amniotic fluid and depressed neonates with APGAR < 7 after 5 min, while induction of labor increased the rate of secondary sections, reduced the rate of spontaneous deliveries, and did not improve perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Induction of labor significantly increased the rate of secondary sections and reduced the rate of spontaneous deliveries, while the percentage of assistant vaginal deliveries was independent from obstetric management and gestational age.
